title: Longest Stable Monitoring Window
description: A monitoring service records latency samples in arrival order. Find the length of the longest contiguous window whose largest and smallest values differ by at most `limit`. The input can be large, so repeatedly scanning an entire window will time out.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the maximum valid window length.
expectedApproach: Maintain a sliding window with a decreasing deque for the maximum and an increasing deque for the minimum. Expand right; while max-min exceeds the limit, advance left and discard expired indices.

publicTests.explanation: The longest windows are [2,4] and [4,7].
[2,4,7,2] has range five.

hiddenTests.explanation: A five-value middle window is valid.

title: Longest Segment Without Repeated Characters
description: Given a single ASCII string, return the length of its longest contiguous substring containing no repeated character. The empty string is valid input.
constraints:
0 <= length <= 200000
Input contains printable ASCII characters and no leading or trailing spaces.
outputFormat: Print the maximum length.
expectedApproach: Track the most recent index of each character. Move the left boundary past a repeated character only when its previous index is still inside the current window.

publicTests.explanation: abc is a longest unique substring.
Only one repeated character can remain.

hiddenTests.explanation: wke is valid; non-contiguous pwke is not.
The left edge must never move backwards.

title: Top K Frequent Values with Deterministic Ties
description: Return the `k` most frequent integers. Sort the answer by descending frequency; when frequencies tie, place the smaller integer first. `k` never exceeds the number of distinct values.
outputFormat: Print the selected values in required order, separated by spaces.
expectedApproach: Count with a map, then either sort distinct entries by the required comparator or keep a size-k heap with the inverse comparator.
expectedTimeComplexity: O(n + u log u) with sorting, or O(n + u log k)

publicTests.explanation: Frequencies are 3, 2, and 1.
The tie is ordered by numeric value.

title: Wait Until a Warmer Reading
description: For each daily temperature, return how many days must pass before a strictly warmer reading. Return `0` when no future day is warmer.
outputFormat: Print `n` wait counts separated by spaces.
expectedApproach: Keep indices of unresolved temperatures in a decreasing stack. A warmer value resolves and pops every smaller temperature on top.

publicTests.explanation: Each answer points to the next strictly warmer day.
Strictly increasing sequence.

title: Search a Rotated Sorted Catalog
description: A strictly increasing array of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown pivot. Return the index of `target` in logarithmic time, or `-1` when absent.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 200000
Values are distinct.
The array is a rotation of a strictly increasing sequence.
outputFormat: Print the zero-based index or `-1`.
expectedApproach: At each binary-search step one half is sorted. Decide whether target lies inside that half; otherwise discard it and search the other half.

publicTests.explanation: Target is after the pivot.
Target is absent.

title: Count Connected Islands
description: A binary grid uses `1` for land and `0` for water. Count connected land components using only horizontal and vertical adjacency. Diagonal cells are not connected.
constraints:
1 <= rows * columns <= 100000
Every row has equal length.
inputFormat:
Line 1: `rows columns`
Next `rows` lines: strings of `0` and `1`
outputFormat: Print the number of islands.
expectedApproach: Scan every cell. On unseen land, increment the count and flood-fill its entire component with iterative DFS or BFS to avoid recursion-depth failures.

publicTests.explanation: Three orthogonally connected components.
No land.

title: Minimum Coins for an Exact Amount
description: Given reusable positive coin denominations and a non-negative amount, return the minimum number of coins whose sum is exactly the amount. Return `-1` when it is impossible.
outputFormat: Print the minimum coin count or `-1`.
expectedApproach: Use one-dimensional DP where dp[x] is the fewest coins for x. Initialize dp[0]=0 and relax every denomination for each reachable amount.

publicTests.explanation: No exact sum exists.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence Length
description: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. Elements do not need to be contiguous. The input size requires better than quadratic time.
outputFormat: Print the subsequence length.
expectedApproach: Maintain tails[len-1], the smallest possible tail for an increasing subsequence of each length. Replace the first tail >= current value using lower_bound.

publicTests.explanation: One LIS is 2,3,7,18.

hiddenTests.explanation: Strict means duplicates do not extend.

title: Minimum Concurrent Meeting Rooms
description: Meetings use half-open intervals `[start, end)`, so a room ending at time `t` can host another meeting starting at `t`. Return the minimum number of rooms needed for every meeting.
outputFormat: Print the minimum room count.
expectedApproach: Sort starts and ends separately and sweep them, releasing rooms when end <= next start; or sort meetings and track active end times in a min-heap.

publicTests.explanation: At most two meetings overlap.
Half-open intervals can reuse the room at ten.

hiddenTests.explanation: One long meeting overlaps a sequential series.

title: Maximum Value in Every Sliding Window
description: For every contiguous window of size `k`, return its maximum value in left-to-right order. The input size rules out sorting each window independently.
outputFormat: Print `n-k+1` maxima separated by spaces.
expectedApproach: Keep indices in a decreasing deque. Remove expired indices from the front and values no larger than the new value from the back; the front is each window maximum.

publicTests.explanation: Maximum for each size-three window.
One window.

title: Median of Two Sorted Streams
description: Given two individually sorted integer arrays, return the median of their combined multiset without merging them. At least one array is non-empty. Print the answer with exactly one decimal place.
constraints:
0 <= n,m <= 200000
1 <= n+m
Values fit in signed 32-bit integers.
Expected logarithmic complexity in the smaller array.
inputFormat:
Line 1: `n m`
Line 2: `n` sorted integers (blank if n=0)
Line 3: `m` sorted integers (blank if m=0)
outputFormat: Print the median with one digit after the decimal point.
expectedApproach: Binary-search a partition in the smaller array so left partitions contain half the elements and both left maxima are <= both right minima. Derive odd/even medians from the boundary values.

publicTests.explanation: Combined order is 1,2,3.
Average of the two middle values.

title: Merge Maintenance Windows
description: A deployment calendar contains inclusive maintenance windows `[start, end]`. Merge every pair that overlaps or touches and return the smallest equivalent list ordered by start time. Your method may reorder the input.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000
0 <= start <= end <= 1000000000
Touching windows, such as [1,3] and [3,5], must merge.
outputFormat: Print each merged window as `start end`, one per line.
expectedApproach: Sort by start, retain the current merged interval, extend its end when the next start is at most the current end, and otherwise emit it.

publicTests.explanation: Overlap and touching are both merged.
A single zero-length window is unchanged.

title: Nearest Available Server
description: A data-center floor is a rectangular grid. `.` is open floor, `#` is blocked, and `S` is an available server. Starting from a given open cell, return the minimum number of orthogonal moves required to reach any server. Return `-1` when no server is reachable.
constraints:
1 <= rows * columns <= 100000
The start is inside the grid and is not blocked.
Moves are up, down, left, and right.
inputFormat:
Line 1: `rows columns`
Next `rows` lines: grid strings
Final line: `startRow startColumn`
outputFormat: Print the minimum number of moves, or `-1`.
expectedApproach: Run BFS from the start, marking cells when enqueued. The first server removed from the queue has minimum distance because BFS processes unweighted paths by level.

publicTests.explanation: The wall forces a route around the lower row.
The start is already a server.

hiddenTests.explanation: Only the lower server is reachable.

title: Minimum Processing Capacity Before Deadline
description: Jobs must be processed in their given order. Each day, a worker handles a consecutive group whose total size does not exceed a fixed daily capacity; a job cannot be split. Return the smallest capacity that finishes all jobs within `days` days.
inputFormat:
Line 1: `n days`
Line 2: `n` positive job sizes
outputFormat: Print the minimum feasible capacity.
expectedApproach: Binary-search between the largest job and the sum of all jobs. A greedy scan computes required days for a candidate capacity; feasibility is monotonic.

publicTests.explanation: Capacity 15 is the smallest five-day schedule.
With one day per job, the maximum job determines capacity.

hiddenTests.explanation: Three jobs must fit on one day.

title: Merge Sorted Log Shards
description: Each server shard returns timestamps in ascending order. Merge all shards into one ascending sequence without first concatenating and globally sorting every value. Empty shards are valid and duplicate timestamps must be preserved.
constraints:
0 <= k <= 10000
Total timestamps <= 200000
Every shard is sorted ascending.
outputFormat: Print merged timestamps separated by spaces. Print an empty line when there are none.

def main() -> None:

title: Bounded Request Deduplicator
description: Events `[requestId, timestamp]` arrive in non-decreasing timestamp order. Accept an event unless the same ID was accepted less than `windowSeconds` earlier. Rejected duplicates do not extend the window. Return one decision per event while evicting old state so memory is bounded by the active window.
constraints:
1 <= windowSeconds <= 86400
1 <= events <= 200000
IDs contain no whitespace and have at most 100 characters.
Timestamps are non-negative and non-decreasing.
outputFormat: Print `true` or `false` for every event on one line, separated by spaces.
examples:
Input
10 3
a 1
a 5
a 11
Output
true false true
expectedApproach: Store the latest accepted timestamp per ID plus a queue of accepted records. Evict records with timestamp <= current-window only if the map still points to that record, then decide and optionally append.
expectedTimeComplexity: O(n) total, amortized O(1) per event

publicTests.explanation: The rejected event at five does not extend the window.
IDs have independent windows; equality is accepted.

hiddenTests.explanation: c at 12 is nine seconds after acceptance.

title: Weighted LRU Cache
description: Implement an LRU cache whose capacity is total weight, not item count. `GET key` returns the value or `-1` and promotes a hit. `PUT key value weight` inserts or replaces an entry, then evicts least-recently-used entries until total weight fits. An entry heavier than the full capacity must not be stored.
constraints:
1 <= capacity <= 1000000
1 <= operations <= 200000
Keys and values are integers.
1 <= weight <= 1000000
Average GET and metadata updates should be O(1).
inputFormat:
Line 1: `capacity operationCount`
Then `GET key` or `PUT key value weight`
outputFormat: Print one line for every GET result.

PUT 2 20 3
GET 1
GET 2
Output
-1
20
expectedApproach: Combine a hash map with a doubly linked list ordered by recency. Track total weight, unlink replacements, reject overweight entries, and evict from the tail until within capacity.
expectedTimeComplexity: O(1) average per GET; amortized O(1) per PUT plus evictions

publicTests.explanation: Adding key two evicts key one.

title: Earliest Pair Matching a Target
description: Return indices `i j` (`i < j`) whose values sum to `target`. Exactly one answer exists. If duplicates permit several answers, choose the pair with the smallest `j`; for that `j`, choose the smallest `i`.
constraints:
2 <= n <= 200000
-1000000000 <= value,target <= 1000000000
Exactly one answer exists under the tie rule.
outputFormat: Print `i j` using zero-based indices.
expectedApproach: Scan left to right while storing the first index for each value. Before inserting the current value, look up target-current. The first match gives the smallest j and retained first index gives the smallest i.

publicTests.explanation: Duplicate values use distinct indices.
